rubrics.title: Lab 10 — Analyze Your Twitter/X Data with Python

criteria.description: Lecture Exercises — lecture10.ipynb: Executed insert/update/delete practice in lab9.demo; saved-query demonstrations; a pandas text table and an aggregation chart or supported empty result. Keep the code and executed outputs. No Summary or AI Use section is required in the lecture notebook.

Independent Questions — lab10.ipynb: Q1–Q4, 10 points each. Each question includes a Markdown heading, the actual MongoDB query in a Markdown code block, runnable Python with pandas output, and a brief Markdown explanation of the actual findings. Q1: up to ten unique most-liked tweets in a complete text/likes table. Q2: up to ten distinct most-followed users in a horizontal bar chart. Q3: common non-empty profile locations counted by distinct users in a bar chart. Q4: stored hashtag occurrences in a bar chart. Use a distinct DataFrame for each question. Correctly executed and explained empty results are acceptable; failed or unexecuted queries are not empty results. No prompt transcript or separate Summary is required.

AI Use — lab10.ipynb only: Identify the approved AI tools actually used, where and how they helped, their limitations, and how their output was checked or corrected. The only approved tools are MongoDB's built-in AI and Gemini inside Colab. Identify reused code or no new AI use honestly. No prompt transcript or separate Summary is required. Confirmed unapproved AI use is governed by the assignment-wide policy, not merely a deduction from this criterion.

Submission & Source Access: Canvas contains exactly two values on separate lines: the assigned GitHub repository root URL and a complete working MongoDB connection string for source-data verification. The repository contains lecture10.ipynb and lab10.ipynb at its root on main, saved directly from Colab with executed outputs, the Created using Colab commit message, and a working Open in Colab button. Credentials belong only in Colab Secrets and the private Canvas submission. Credential exposure is a separate one-time 20-point deduction from the otherwise earned assignment score, floored at zero; do not deduct again under this criterion for the same exposure.
